question: Which integrated phononic devices have been realized?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: Answer identifies the phononic integrated circuit platform realized on GaN-on-sapphire and enumerates its demonstrated passive components: low-loss single-mode phononic waveguides, chip-to-cable connectors, evanescent directional couplers, and waveguide-coupled high-Q acoustic ring resonators.
examples: Waveguides, connectors, couplers, and high-Q ring resonators were all integrated on GaN-on-sapphire
High-Q ring resonators coupled to waveguides complete the basic PnIC

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: Answer includes the adiabatic phononic mode converter: a tapered phononic waveguide exploiting substrate anisotropy to convert quasi-Rayleigh to quasi-Love modes with >96% efficiency, GHz-band operation (~1.44 GHz 3 dB bandwidth), and tolerance to fabrication errors.
examples: A tapered waveguide achieves adiabatic Rayleigh-to-Love conversion exceeding 96% efficiency
The converter is broadband (1.44 GHz 3 dB bandwidth) and robust to fabrication errors

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: Answer includes the realized phonon beam splitter, characterized with single phonons using two superconducting qubits and shown to preserve quantum behavior via two-phonon interference.
examples: A beam splitter was fully characterized using single phonons and two superconducting qubits
Two-phonon interference was demonstrated through the beam splitter

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: Answer frames the realized devices as passive phononic integrated components that mirror photonic integrated circuit elements (waveguides, couplers, resonators), replicating basic PIC functionalities.
examples: The PnIC architecture is an acoustic analog of PICs
These passive components mirror waveguides, couplers, and resonators from integrated photonics

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: Answer mentions the platform's compatibility with PICs for on-chip phonon-photon coupling and quantum links between superconducting qubits and optical fields, or improved performance in cryogenic environments.
examples: Phonons and photons can be coupled on a single chip via optoacoustic interaction
Cryogenic operation paves the way for interfacing superconducting quantum devices

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: Answer notes that the ring resonator geometry gives rise to coupling between phonon orbital angular momentum and spin, enabling gyroscopic or non-reciprocal devices.
examples: Ring geometry couples phonon OAM and spin
This opens doors to acoustic gyroscopes and non-reciprocal devices

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: Answer notes that confining phonons in small volume with long lifetime and routing them in circuits enhances conventional acoustic sensing devices.
examples: Long-lifetime, small-volume phonon confinement enhances acoustic sensing
Complex phononic routing improves sensor versatility

ingredients.name: valuable_3
ingredients.criterion: Answer notes that the mode converter and beam splitter serve both classical and quantum phononic information processing, e.g., linear mechanical quantum computing and conversion between itinerant phonons and superconducting qubits.
examples: The beam splitter supports linear mechanical quantum computing with phonons
Straightforward conversion between itinerant phonons and superconducting qubits
